answer: Sybil resistance requires each identity to complete a publicly verifiable VDF: every modular squaring depends on the previous one, imposing elapsed time that GPUs cannot remove for a single instance. An attacker can run clone proofs in parallel, but must spend hardware and time on each clone. A Wesolowski proof lets verifiers check completion efficiently. Like following a river past an oasis, pigment marks each sequential step, not a shortcut.
